match.reason: The new point teaches Leslie matrices, a population projection model using birth and survival rates by age group, which is a different idea from the geometric transformations taught by the bank point.

draft.title: Leslie matrices
card: A Leslie matrix models a population split into age groups. The state matrix lists the number in each age group, youngest first.

The top row holds birth rates: the average number of young born to each member of an age group. Entries just below the main diagonal hold survival rates: the proportion of one age group that moves up to the next. All other entries are 0.
The next population is L × S, found the same way as with any transition matrix. Add the groups to get the total population.
draft.remember: Top row: births. Below the diagonal: survival to the next age group.

a.q: A Leslie matrix is L = [0 2 1; 0.5 0 0; 0 0.4 0]. What does the 0.4 in row 3, column 2 mean?
opts: Proportion of age group 2 that survive into group 3
Average births per member of age group 2
Proportion of age group 3 that survive another step
Proportion of age group 3 born to group 2
a.why: An entry below the diagonal is a survival rate from one age group to the next. Column 2 is the group that starts and row 3 is where it ends up. Births appear only in the top row.
a.clue: It is not in the top row, so it is not about births.

b.q: A population has L = [0 1.5 1; 0.6 0 0; 0 0.5 0] and S = [80; 50; 20], with age groups youngest first. What is the total population after one step?
b.why: Youngest = 1.5×50 + 1×20 = 95. Second = 0.6×80 = 48. Oldest = 0.5×50 = 25. The total is 95 + 48 + 25 = 168. The option 73 leaves out the new births, and 150 is the starting total.
b.clue: Work out all three groups, then add them.

a.best: Proportion of age group 2 that survive into group 3

problems.detail: "found the same way as with any transition matrix" suggests a Leslie matrix is a transition matrix. Point 1 defines a transition matrix as one whose columns give chances of moving between states, and a Leslie matrix's columns do not do that or sum to 1. Better: "found by matrix multiplication, as with a transition matrix".

check.summary: Both answers check out: a is the survival rate from group 2 to group 3, and b is 168. One small wording issue: the card implies a Leslie matrix is a kind of transition matrix, which clashes with point 1's definition.
